Yes, diabetes mellitus can influence the efficacy of FDG-PET in the diagnosis of cervical cancer. 

FDG-PET (Fluorodeoxyglucose-Positron Emission Tomography) relies on the uptake of glucose by cells, with cancer cells typically exhibiting higher glucose uptake due to their increased metabolic rate. However, in patients with diabetes mellitus, the elevated blood glucose levels can compete with the FDG uptake, potentially reducing the sensitivity and specificity of the scan. This is because the high blood glucose levels can lead to decreased FDG uptake in cancer cells, making it more challenging to distinguish between malignant and benign tissues.

As a result, diabetes mellitus may affect the accuracy of FDG-PET scans in diagnosing cervical cancer, potentially leading to false-negative results. Therefore, it is essential to consider a patient's diabetic status and blood glucose levels when interpreting FDG-PET scan results for cervical cancer diagnosis.
